summary: Bernhard Breloer was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Jena, Bonn (Ph.D., Dr.iuris), Berlin, and Munich under Hermann Jacobi, Willibald Kirfel, Josef Partsch, and Wilhelm Geiger. He held posts at Bonn (1927) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1935).

Bernhard Forssman is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1955-1964) and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968-1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Iranian, Indological, and linguistic studies. He studied at Vienna (Ph.D.), Prague, Heidelberg under Franz Kielhorn, Bonn, and Göttingen. He held posts at Vienna (1909, 1919-1938), the Asia Institute (1938-1950), and Columbia University (1951-1956).

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at the Carolinum and University of Zurich, Berlin under Franz Bopp, Göttingen (Ph.D.), and Paris under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as reader (1833), Docent (1835-1837), and Privatdozent (1845) at Zurich.

Bernhard Jülg was a scholar of linguistics and Central Asian studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Berlin (under Boeckh, Bopp, Lachmann, Petermann, Schott), and Kiel (Ph.D.). He held professorships at Lviv (1851), Jagiellonian University (1853), and Innsbruck (1863).

Bernhard Karlgren was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1907-1915). He later held academic posts at Uppsala University (~1915-1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918-1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt (Ph.D. under Werner Thomas), and Cologne (PhD, Habilitation). His main posts included the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1970-1972), Kiel (1974-1993), and Leipzig (1993-2001).

Bernie Glassman was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at NYU, Brooklyn Poly, and UCLA (Ph.D. in mathematics), and trained under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Bert Vaux is a linguist who studied at the University of Chicago (BA 1986-1990) and Harvard University (MA 1990-1994). He has held faculty posts at Harvard (2000-2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003-2006), and the University of Cambridge (2006-2010, 2021).

Berthe Jansen is a tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied at Leiden University (BA, PhD under Jonathan A. Silk) and Oxford (MPhil). She held posts at Leiden University (2015-2016) and Heidelberg University (~2015-2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Halle, studying under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Heymann Steinthal. He held posts at Halle (1867) and Jena (1870-1913).

Berthold Laufer was a sinologist and tibetologist. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig (Ph.D. under August Conrady). He served at the American Museum of Natural History (1901-1906), Columbia University (1905-1907), and the Field Museum of Natural History (from 1907).

Bertram Fulke Hartshorne was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his secondary education at Charterhouse School (~1858-1863) and studied at Pembroke College, Oxford, receiving a B.A. (~1864-1868).

Bertram G. Liyanage works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at Savitribai Phule Pune University (2013-2015) and served at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and Temple University (2022).

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied traditionally under Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied in Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, Munich (doctorate), and under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at BHU, Alice Boner Institute, Vienna, and Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She earned a Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama. She served as a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy, studying at Heidelberg, Bonn, Göttingen, Kiel, and Halle under Jacobi, Oldenberg, Deussen, Sieg, and Hultzsch. She held posts at Halle, Hamburg, SOAS, Oxford, and the University of Ceylon.
Betty Jean Shefts is a scholar in the fields of linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied under Franklin Edgerton, Paul Thieme, and Geshe Nornang.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman at the Lotus Research Centre.
